tools.name: luckdrop_check_entry
tools.description:

Sourced from the CHAIN rather than our database, because this gates a transaction
and a stale yes costs the caller gas on a revert.

Returns canEnter, a reason mirroring the contract's own revert strings, and the

tools.name: luckdrop_get_results
tools.description:
Read a single draw's five rounds and its winner.

`week` is the DISPLAY week number by default. If you are following contractWeekId
from the chain, pass idSpace='contract' -- the same number means different draws
in the two id spaces, and without it you get a valid-looking answer describing the
WRON

tools.description:

the trading window is currently open. Tickets are NFTs and can be traded while a
draw is running.

tools.name: luckdrop_check_prize
tools.description:
Check whether a wallet has won a prize it has not yet collected, and get the
transaction that claims it. Read from the chain, so it works for a wallet that
entered without ever signing in to the website.

SCOPE: this reads THIS DEPLOYMENT's prize escrows, and the result names in
escrowsChecked exact

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: luckdrop_get_draw, luckdrop_list_market · Private data: luckdrop_get_draw, luckdrop_check_entry, luckdrop_list_market, luckdrop_check_prize · Public sink: luckdrop_check_entry, luckdrop_check_prize · Destructive: luckdrop_check_prize.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: luckdrop_get_draw, luckdrop_list_market · Private data: luckdrop_get_draw, luckdrop_check_entry, luckdrop_list_market, luckdrop_check_prize · Public sink: luckdrop_check_entry, luckdrop_check_prize · Destructive: luckdrop_check_prize

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
